name: CA-27
label: Safe D

key_factors: Whitesides holds a roughly 10-to-1 fundraising edge with $2.5M on hand versus Gibbs' $200K
D+6 district with a first-term Democratic incumbent and no outside spending against him

model.rationale: The incumbent's overwhelming financial advantage, a D+6 seat, minimal outside opposition, and market pricing near 96% all point to a comfortable Democratic hold. With no polls available, fundamentals carry the forecast, and they favor Whitesides decisively.
model.watch: A late wave of Republican outside spending or a national environment breaking sharply toward the GOP could narrow the margin considerably.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Incumbent George T. Whitesides (D) is running.

overview:
California's 27th District leans Democratic by six points, and first-term incumbent George Whitesides returns with the advantages of incumbency and a dominant war chest. He has raised about $4 million and holds $2.5 million on hand, while Republican Jason Gibbs has raised under $400,000 with roughly $200,000 available. Outside groups have spent very little, and no meaningful opposition advertising has materialized.

Prediction markets give Whitesides roughly a 96 percent chance of reelection, and no public polls or expert ratings complicate the picture. The combination of a favorable district, a well-funded incumbent, and an under-resourced challenger points to a comfortable Democratic hold, though the absence of polling leaves some room for surprise.
